author: Linnaeus, 1758
status: 나그네새 10만 마리 이상 · 겨울철새 수만 마리 · 여름에도 드물게 기록

months.note: 봄(3~5월)과 가을(8~11월)에 많이 지나가고 겨울에도 많이 머물며 6월에는 드물고, 번식지에서는 5월 중순~6월 중순에 알을 낳는다.

summary: 국내를 흔히 지나가는 나그네새이며, 일부는 무리를 지어 갯벌과 강 하구에서 겨울을 난다. 갯벌·간척지·염전 등에 찾아오며, 우리나라에서 겨울을 나는 도요새 가운데 가장 대표적인 종이다. 조개, 달팽이, 갑각류, 지렁이, 거미, 곤충을 먹는다. 유라시아와 북아메리카 대륙의 한대에서 번식해 관목이나 풀뿌리 사이 오목한 곳의 접시 모양 둥지에 알 4개를 낳고, 우리나라 서남해 연안과 섬, 일본, 중국에서 겨울을 난다.

sexes.text: 암수 생김새가 같고 암컷이 조금 더 크며 부리가 더 길다.

young: 어린새는 윗면 깃에 붉은 갈색~담황색 가장자리가 있고, 담황색 가슴에 가는 줄무늬가 있으며, 배와 옆구리에 검은 점무늬가 흩어져 있다(배 한가운데의 큰 검은 반점은 없다).

similar.how: 민물도요는 다리가 짧고 부리 끝만 살짝 굽으며 허리 가운데가 검어, 다리가 길고 부리가 고르게 굽었으며 허리가 흰 붉은갯도요와 다르다.

art.subject: Dunlin (Calidris alpina), adult in winter (non-breeding) plumage, as seen on Korean tidal flats from October to March: plain grey-brown upperparts with fine dark shaft streaks, head and neck grey-brown with a faint whitish supercilium, a soft grey-brown wash and fine streaks across the breast, the rest of the underparts clean white; black bill; dark eye; black legs.
art.pose: walking on wet mud at the edge of a dense winter flock, head raised in side view so the whole bill is clearly visible; every bird in the flock is in the same plain grey winter plumage
art.scene: Korean south-west coast tidal flat in winter, wide mudflat near a river mouth; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding plumage (April–May), side view standing: bright rufous back and crown with black feather centres, finely streaked whitish breast, large solid black patch on the belly, black bill only a little longer than the head and drooping slightly at the tip, black legs

adult winter plumage, side view standing: plain pale grey-brown upperparts with no rufous and no dark scaly centres, soft grey-brown wash and faint fine streaks on the breast, all-white belly, the same short, gently drooping black bill, black legs
art.build: Small, compact, round-bodied sandpiper, 17–21cm, a little larger than a sparrow; short neck, rather hunched when feeding. Bill black, about 1.2 to 1.3 times the head length (bill base to back of the head, never close to twice), fairly thick at the base, straight for the first two-thirds and drooping gently only in the outer third; not an evenly curved, curlew-like bill. Legs black, medium length. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. In flight a narrow white wing-bar and a dark centre to the rump and tail with white sides.
avoid: Do not paint a long, evenly curved bill — that is Curlew Sandpiper (Calidris ferruginea); the Dunlin's bill is only a little longer than the head and droops only near the tip.
Do not give it a white rump patch (Curlew Sandpiper).
Do not show the black belly patch or rufous back on winter birds; they are breeding plumage only.
Do not paint winter birds brown, scaly or heavily streaked; they are plain grey above with only faint breast streaks.
Do not paint greenish or yellow legs.
Do not curve the bill from its base; it is straight for two-thirds of its length and droops only near the tip.
